ObjectivePhase.description:
Kill chain phases for objective ordering.

Practical 5-phase model aligned with sub-agent routing:
  recon          → recon agent       (TA0043 Reconnaissance)
  initial-access → exploit agent     (TA0001 Initial Access + TA0002 Execution)
  post-exploit   → postexploit agent (TA0003-TA0009: Persistence thru Collection)
  c2             → postexploit agent (TA0011 Command and Control)
  exfiltration   → postexploit agent (TA0010 Exfiltration + Actions on Objectives)
ObjectivePhase.title: ObjectivePhase

EffectClass.description:
Blast-radius class of an objective — drives fan-out admission (ADR-0077).

The generic dispatch gate compares this across in-flight work units:
``read`` units may overlap freely, ``mutate`` units serialize on shared
resources, ``destructive`` units run alone and only in a mission-
sanctioned final phase. Unset on the objective means ``MUTATE`` —
unknown is always treated conservatively.
EffectClass.title: EffectClass

Objective.description:
A single engagement objective — analogous to ralph's user story.

Each objective must be completable in ONE agent context window.
The ralph loop picks the highest-priority objective whose status is not completed.

acceptance_criteria.description: Verifiable criteria — each must be checkable
acceptance_criteria.title: Acceptance Criteria

priority.description: Execution order (1 = first). Respects kill chain dependencies.
priority.title: Priority

opsec.description: OPSEC posture — drives tool selection and detection avoidance rigor

opsec_notes.description: Specific OPSEC constraints for this objective
opsec_notes.title: Opsec Notes

concessions.description: Pre-authorized assists if objective is blocked (TIBER/CORIE concept)
concessions.title: Concessions

effects.description: Blast-radius class for fan-out admission (ADR-0077); unset means MUTATE — unknown is treated conservatively

resources.description: Shared mutable resources this objective touches, e.g. 'account:svc', 'host:10.0.0.5', 'surface:/api/Users' — admission serializes concurrent mutating work on the same resource
resources.title: Resources

parallel_safe.description: True when declared safe to run concurrently with other work; False forces serialization; None (unset) is treated as False for mutating work
parallel_safe.title: Parallel Safe

fragile_target.description: True when the target resource is known fragile (embedded device, single-worker service, lockout-sensitive account): admission keeps its in-flight unit count at per_target_max permanently, bypassing progressive widening (ADR-0077)
fragile_target.title: Fragile Target

blocked_by.description: Objective IDs that must complete first
blocked_by.title: Blocked By

parent_id.description: Optional parent objective ID. When set, this objective is a sub-task of the parent — the parent cannot move to COMPLETED until every child is COMPLETED or CANCELLED. Inspired by PentestGPT's Pentesting Task Tree (PTT).
parent_id.title: Parent Id

OpsecLevel.description:
OPSEC posture for an objective.

Determines C2 tier selection, tool choices, and detection avoidance rigor.
Based on Red Team Maturity Model levels and C2 tier mapping.
See docs/red-team/opplan-domain-knowledge.md for details.
OpsecLevel.title: OpsecLevel

opplan.description:
Operations Plan — the tactical task tracker for the ralph loop.

Direct analogue of ralph's prd.json. The autonomous loop reads this
file each iteration, picks the next objective, executes it, and
updates the status.

Hierarchical mode: any objective with ``parent_id`` set becomes a
child of that parent. Trees are arbitrary depth — but real plans
rarely need more than two levels in practice. The flat-list code
paths still work when no hierarchy is set.

threat_profile.description: Short threat actor summary for context injection each iteration
threat_profile.title: Threat Profile

opplan.title: OPPLAN

FindingConfidence.description: Confidence level for a finding — drives verification requirements.
FindingConfidence.title: FindingConfidence

Adversary tier — numeric grading aligned with the threat-profile
skill (Tier 1–4). Distinct from ``ThreatActor.sophistication``,
which stays as the free-form CONOPS embedded field.
ThreatTier.title: ThreatTier

threat-profile.description:
Adversary persona for emulation — stored at ``plan/threat-profile.json``.

Distinct from ``CONOPS.threat_actors`` (embedded), this is the
standalone JSON the orchestrator's OPPLAN-builder consults to choose
TTP sequences and the operations agents consult to bound tool
selection. One profile per engagement; multi-actor scenarios should
pick the dominant emulation target.

actor_name.description: Primary actor identifier, e.g. 'APT29-like (Cozy Bear)' or 'Custom — Insider'
actor_name.title: Actor Name

group_id.description: MITRE Groups ID if known, e.g. 'G0050'
group_id.title: Group Id

key_ttps.description: Top 5–10 MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs this actor relies on
key_ttps.title: Key Ttps

tools.description: Realistic toolset for emulation (e.g. Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, custom RAT)
tools.title: Tools

infrastructure.description: C2 patterns, VPS providers, domain naming heuristics
infrastructure.title: Infrastructure

recent_cti_delta.description: Free-text summary of CTI deltas from the most recent 12 months
recent_cti_delta.title: Recent Cti Delta

confidence.description: Confidence that the live actor matches this profile

threat-profile.title: ThreatProfile

Contact.description: A single human contact reachable by the agent or operator.
Contact.title: Contact

contact.description:
Operator + escalation + abort channels — ``plan/contact.json``.

Designed for autonomous-AI engagements where the agent itself is the
"red cell" and only humans staff the white / blue cells. Full
multi-cell rosters belong in an external comms doc.

escalation_chain.description: Ordered list — agent escalates down this chain when the primary operator is unreachable past the abort_plan's response window.
escalation_chain.title: Escalation Chain

abort_signal_recipient.description: Who the agent pages on EMERGENCY-severity abort triggers

external_soc_endpoint.description: Optional webhook the agent POSTs to before active scanning (deconfliction notice). Empty = no external SOC integration.
external_soc_endpoint.title: External Soc Endpoint

blackout_windows.description: ISO 8601 datetime ranges (e.g. '2026-05-21T22:00:00+09:00/PT8H') during which the agent must not run active operations
blackout_windows.title: Blackout Windows

contact.title: ContactPlan

DataClass.description: A single category of data the agent may encounter or collect.

retention_days.description: Days to keep collected evidence of this class before automatic purge
retention_days.title: Retention Days

handling_notes.description: Class-specific rules, e.g. 'redact PII before quoting in findings', 'never store cleartext credentials — hash with bcrypt before logging'
handling_notes.title: Handling Notes

DataClass.title: DataClass

data-handling.description:
Evidence storage + chain-of-custody — ``plan/data-handling.json``.

Default ``data_classes`` cover credentials / PII / source-code with
conservative retention; engagements with compliance requirements
(GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS) override via the interview.

default.name: credentials
default.handling_notes: Hash before logging; never quote cleartext in findings.

default.name: pii
default.handling_notes: Redact PII fields in findings; aggregate before reporting.

default.name: source-code
default.handling_notes: OK to quote relevant snippets in findings under fair use.

default.name: business-data
default.handling_notes: Do not export beyond the engagement workspace; summarize only.

evidence_storage_path.description: Engagement-workspace-relative path where collected evidence is stored
evidence_storage_path.title: Evidence Storage Path

chain_of_custody.description: If True, every evidence file gets a SHA-256 hash recorded in the Finding
chain_of_custody.title: Chain Of Custody

purge_after_days.description: Hard cap — every artifact in evidence/ older than this is purged regardless of data_class.retention_days
purge_after_days.title: Purge After Days

compliance_frameworks.description: Frameworks that bind this engagement: GDPR / HIPAA / PCI-DSS / SOC2 / etc.
compliance_frameworks.title: Compliance Frameworks

data-handling.title: DataHandlingPlan

AbortTrigger.description: A single condition that, when matched, triggers the response_action.

condition.description: Concrete condition, e.g. 'SOC issues real-incident alert', 'real production data observed in scan output', 'scope boundary violation detected'
condition.title: Condition

response_action.description: Agent's mandated action, e.g. 'halt current objective, snapshot workspace, notify operator within 60s'
response_action.title: Response Action

auto_halt.description: Whether the agent halts itself on detection (True) or only flags the trigger and awaits operator decision (False)
auto_halt.title: Auto Halt

AbortTrigger.title: AbortTrigger

TriggerSeverity.description: Severity tier for an abort trigger — drives the agent's response.
TriggerSeverity.title: TriggerSeverity

abort.description:
Halt-trigger roster + AI-aware safety gates — ``plan/abort.json``.

AI-specific fields (``hallucination_threshold``, ``destructive_action_gate``,
``output_validation``) defend against the LLM-driven failure modes
documented in OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2025.12).

default.condition: Real-incident alert from blue team / SOC
default.response_action: Halt all agents; preserve evidence; notify operator immediately

default.condition: Production data observed in collected evidence
default.response_action: Halt active objective; quarantine evidence; await operator
Halt active objective; document the violation; await operator

abort_signal_channel.description: Operator-side mechanism to signal abort (file marker, HTTP endpoint, ask_user_question response). Empty = no out-of-band abort channel; operator pauses via CLI Ctrl+C only.
abort_signal_channel.title: Abort Signal Channel

recovery_procedure.default: After abort: snapshot workspace; export evidence with chain-of-custody; run cleanup.json removal commands; require operator approval before resume.
recovery_procedure.title: Recovery Procedure

hallucination_threshold.description: Count of consecutive unverified-success claims before the agent is forced into evidence-collection mode rather than progress
hallucination_threshold.title: Hallucination Threshold

destructive_action_gate.description: If True, every command flagged as destructive (rm -rf, drop table, format, ...) must pass verify-before-run policy. Disable only for read-only engagements.
destructive_action_gate.title: Destructive Action Gate

output_validation.description: Method used to validate agent-reported successes: 'verify-evidence-hash' (sha256 every artifact), 'second-tool-confirm' (re-run with different tool), 'operator-spot-check' (ask_user_question)
output_validation.title: Output Validation

abort.title: AbortPlan

CleanupArtifact.description:
Single artifact the agent created on a target during the engagement.

Filled in mostly during execution (by the operations agents) but
Soundwave seeds the plan with the expected categories based on the
CONOPS kill chain so each phase has a place to record what it
touched.

artifact_type.description: Category: beacon / account / file / scheduled-task / service / registry-key / persistence-mechanism / tool / network-rule
artifact_type.title: Artifact Type

host.description: Hostname, IP, or asset identifier where the artifact lives
host.title: Host

path.description: File path, registry key, account name, or other concrete locator
path.title: Path

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the artifact when it's a file
sha256.title: Sha256

persistence_mech.description: If this is a persistence implant: which mech (scheduled-task, service, registry-run, cron, systemd-unit, ...)
persistence_mech.title: Persistence Mech

removal_command.description: Concrete command to remove the artifact (idempotent if possible)
removal_command.title: Removal Command

verifier_command.description: Command whose zero exit confirms removal
verifier_command.title: Verifier Command

created_by_objective.description: OPPLAN objective ID that created this artifact
created_by_objective.title: Created By Objective

CleanupArtifact.title: CleanupArtifact

cleanup.description:
Post-engagement cleanup roster — ``plan/cleanup.json``.

Replaces ``RoE.cleanup_required`` (deprecated bool flag). The
orchestrator and operations agents append to ``artifacts`` as they
create persistent state on targets; the engagement is not "complete"
until every artifact has ``removed=True`` or has an explicit
``cancellation_reason`` recorded.

completion_criteria.default: All listed artifacts have removed=True OR a documented cancellation_reason (e.g. operator decided to leave a honeyfile for blue team training).
completion_criteria.title: Completion Criteria

pre_engagement_baseline.description: Reference to a pre-engagement system snapshot or backup (volume ID, snapshot timestamp, restore command) so the operator can roll back if cleanup is incomplete.
pre_engagement_baseline.title: Pre Engagement Baseline

cleanup.title: CleanupPlan
